evidence.pali: 208 . ‘‘Tassa mayhaṃ, bhikkhave, evaṃ appamattassa ātāpino pahitattassa viharato uppajjati byāpādavitakko…pe… uppajjati vihiṃsāvitakko. So evaṃ pajānāmi – ‘uppanno kho me ayaṃ vihiṃsāvitakko. So ca kho attabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, parabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, ubhayabyābādhāyapi saṃvattati, paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṃvattaniko’. ‘Attabyābādhāya saṃvattatī’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṃ gacchati; ‘parabyābādhāya saṃvattatī’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṃ gacchati; ‘ubhayabyābādhāya saṃvattatī’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṃ gacchati; ‘paññānirodhiko vighātapakkhiko anibbānasaṃvattaniko’tipi me, bhikkhave, paṭisañcikkhato abbhatthaṃ gacchati. So kho ahaṃ, bhikkhave, uppannuppannaṃ vihiṃsāvitakkaṃ pajahameva vinodameva byantameva naṃ akāsiṃ.
evidence.chinese_simplified: 208. “诸比丘，当我如此不放逸、热忱、自我策励地安住时，生起了瞋寻……乃至……生起了害寻。我这样了知：‘我生起了这个害寻。它既导致恼害自己，也导致恼害他人，还导致恼害双方；它障碍智慧，是苦恼品类，不导向涅槃。’诸比丘，当我反思‘它导致恼害自己’时，它就消失了；诸比丘，当我反思‘它导致恼害他人’时，它就消失了；诸比丘，当我反思‘它导致恼害双方’时，它就消失了；诸比丘，当我反思‘它障碍智慧，是苦恼品类，不导向涅槃’时，它就消失了。诸比丘，我就是这样，对每一个生起的害寻，都予以舍断、去除、灭尽。”
evidence.english: 208. “Monks, as I was dwelling thus—heedful, ardent, and resolute—a thought of ill will arose in me… a thought of violence arose in me. I understood it thus: ‘This thought of violence has arisen in me. It leads to my own affliction, to the affliction of others, and to the affliction of both; it obstructs wisdom, is on the side of distress, and does not lead to Nibbāna.’ As I reflected, ‘It leads to my own affliction,’ it subsided in me. As I reflected, ‘It leads to the affliction of others,’ it subsided in me. As I reflected, ‘It leads to the affliction of both,’ it subsided in me. As I reflected, ‘It obstructs wisdom, is on the side of distress, and does not lead to Nibbāna,’ it subsided in me. Monks, I would abandon, dispel, and make an end of each thought of violence as it arose.

entries.work_title: 分别论义注迷惑冰消 Sammohavinodanī-Aṭṭhakathā
entries.pali: 181 . Tatiyachakke kāmo ti dve kāmā – vatthukāmo ca kilesakāmo ca. Tattha kilesakāmaṃ sandhāya kāmapaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu kāmadhātu, kāmavitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Vatthukāmaṃ sandhāya kāmoyeva dhātu kāmadhātu, kāmāvacaradhammānametaṃ nāmaṃ. Byāpādapaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu byāpādadhātu, byāpādavitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Byāpādova dhātu byāpādadhātu, dasaāghātavatthukassa paṭighassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Vihiṃsā paṭisaṃyuttā dhātu vihiṃsādhātu, vihiṃsāvitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Vihiṃsāyeva dhātu vihiṃsādhātu, parasattavihesanassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Ayaṃ pana heṭṭhā anāgatattā evaṃ atthādivibhāgato veditabbā – vihiṃsanti etāya satte, vihiṃsanaṃ vā etaṃ sattānanti vihiṃsā. Sā viheṭhanalakkhaṇā, karuṇāpaṭipakkhalakkhaṇā vā; parasantāne ubbegajananarasā, sakasantāne karuṇāviddhaṃsanarasā vā; dukkhāyatanapaccupaṭṭhānā; paṭighapadaṭṭhānāti veditabbā. Nekkhammaṃ vuccati lobhā nikkhantattā alobho, nīvaraṇehi nikkhantattā paṭhamajjhānaṃ, sabbākusalehi nikkhantattā sabbakusalaṃ. Nekkhammapaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu nekkhammadhātu, nekkhammavitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Nekkhammameva dhātu nekkhammadhātu, sabbassāpi kusalassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Abyāpādapaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu abyāpādadhātu, abyāpādavitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Abyāpādova dhātu abyāpādadhātu, mettāyetaṃ nāmaṃ. Avihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyuttā dhātu avihiṃsādhātu, avihiṃsā vitakkassetaṃ nāmaṃ. Avihiṃsāva dhātu avihiṃsādhātu, karuṇāyetaṃ nāmaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 181. 于第三组六界中，欲有两种：事欲(vatthukāma)与烦恼欲(kilesakāma)。其中，与烦恼欲相应的界为欲界，此是欲寻之名。与事欲相应者，欲本身即是界，为欲界，此是欲界诸法之名。与瞋相应的界为瞋界，此是瞋寻之名。瞋本身即是界，为瞋界，此是十愤恨事之名。与害相应的界为害界，此是害寻之名。害本身即是界，为害界，此是恼害他有情之名。此“害”因前文未述，故当从义理等方面作此分别：以其伤害有情，或对有情的伤害，故为“害”。其特征为恼害，或与悲相反；作用为于他人生起怖畏，或于自身毁坏悲心；现起为苦的依处；近因为瞋，当如是了知。出离，因出离贪欲，故为无贪；因出离诸盖，故为初禅；因出离一切不善法，故为一切善法。与出离相应的界为出离界，此是出离寻之名。出离本身即是界，为出离界，此是一切善法之名。与无瞋相应的界为无瞋界，此是无瞋寻之名。无瞋本身即是界，为无瞋界，此是慈之名。与无害相应的界为无害界，此是无害寻之名。无害本身即是界，为无害界，此是悲之名。
entries.english: 181. In the third set of six, 'sensual desire' (kāma) refers to two kinds of sensual desire: sensual objects (vatthukāma) and defilement-sensual desire (kilesakāma). Herein, with reference to defilement-sensual desire, the element associated with sensual desire is the sensual-desire element (kāmadhātu); this is a name for sensual thought (kāmavitakka). With reference to sensual objects, the element that is simply sensual desire is the sensual-desire element; this is a name for phenomena of the sense-sphere (kāmāvacaradhammā). The element associated with ill will is the ill-will element (byāpādadhātu); this is a name for ill-will thought (byāpādavitakka). The element that is simply ill will is the ill-will element; this is a name for aversion (paṭigha) based on the ten grounds for anger (dasa āghātavatthu). The element associated with cruelty is the cruelty element (vihiṃsādhātu); this is a name for cruelty thought (vihiṃsāvitakka). The element that is simply cruelty is the cruelty element; this is a name for the tormenting of other beings (parasattavihesana). This, however, as it has not been mentioned before, should be understood by way of its division into meaning, and so forth: 'vihiṃsā' means that by which beings are harmed, or it is the harming of beings. It has the characteristic of injuring, or the characteristic of being the antithesis of compassion; its function is to generate agitation in the continuity of others, or to destroy compassion in one's own continuity; it manifests as a basis for suffering; and it has aversion (paṭigha) as its proximate cause. 'Renunciation' (nekkhamma) is said to be non-greed because of having departed from greed, the first jhāna because of having departed from the hindrances, and all that is wholesome because of having departed from all that is unwholesome. The element associated with renunciation is the renunciation element (nekkhammadhātu); this is a name for renunciation thought (nekkhammavitakka). The element that is simply renunciation is the renunciation element; this is a name for all that is wholesome (sabbakusala). The element associated with non-ill-will is the non-ill-will element (abyāpādadhātu); this is a name for non-ill-will thought (abyāpādavitakka). The element that is simply non-ill-will is the non-ill-will element; this is a name for loving-kindness (mettā). The element associated with non-cruelty is the non-cruelty element (avihiṃsādhātu); this is a name for non-cruelty thought (avihiṃsāvitakka). The element that is simply non-cruelty is the non-cruelty element; this is a name for compassion (karuṇā).

entries.pali: 869 . Samathabala nti kāmacchandādike paccanīkadhamme sametīti samatho, so eva paṭipakkhehi akampiyaṭṭhena balaṃ. Aniccādivasena vividhehi ākārehi passatīti vipassanā, sā eva vuttanayena balanti vipassanābalaṃ. Nekkhammavasenā tiādīsu kāmacchandavikkhambhanassa nekkhammasaṅkappassa, alobhapadhānassa vā tathāpavattakusalacittuppādassa vasena cittassa ekaggatāsaṅkhāto yo avikkhepo, taṃ samathabalaṃ . Byāpādavikkhambhanassa abyāpādavitakkassa, adosapadhānassa vā tathāpavattakusalacittuppādassa vaseneva. Thinamiddhavikkhambhikāya vibhūtaṃ katvā manasikaraṇena upaṭṭhitaālokasaññāya vasena. Uddhaccavikkhambhanassa avikkhepassa samādhānassa vasena. Sakalamicchāvitakkavikkhambhanassa sikhāpattaānāpānassatisiddhapaṭinissaggānupassiassāsapassāsānaṃ vasena cittassa ekaggatāsaṅkhāto yo avikkhepo, taṃ samathabala nti atthayojanā.
entries.chinese_simplified: 869. 所谓止力，是指能平息欲贪等敌对之法，故为止；此止因不为敌对法所动摇，故为力。所谓观力，是指以无常等种种行相而观，故为观(vipassanā)；此观如前述，亦为力，故为观力。于出离等中，依于镇伏欲贪的出离思惟，或依无贪为主导而如是生起之善心，其心之不散乱，即所谓的心一境性，此为止力。依于镇伏瞋恚的无瞋寻，或依无瞋为主导而如是生起之善心，亦复如是。依于镇伏惛沉睡眠的、通过清晰作意而现起的光明想。依于镇伏掉举的不散乱，即定。为镇伏一切邪寻，依于由已达究竟之入出息念(ānāpānassati)所成就的、随观舍遣的入出息，其心之不散乱，即所谓的心一境性，此为止力。此为义理的结合。
entries.english: 869. The power of tranquility (samathabala): It pacifies opposing states such as sensual desire; thus, it is tranquility (samatha). That very tranquility is power (bala) in the sense of being unshakable by opposing forces. The power of insight (vipassanābala): It sees in various ways by means of impermanence and so forth; thus, it is insight (vipassanā). That very insight is power (bala) in the manner stated. In the passage beginning 'by way of renunciation,' the power of tranquility is that non-distraction of the mind, termed one-pointedness. It is established by means of the thought of renunciation which suppresses sensual desire, or by means of the arising of wholesome consciousness predominated by non-greed that occurs in such a way; by means of the thought of non-ill will which suppresses ill will, or by means of the arising of wholesome consciousness predominated by non-aversion that occurs in such a way; by means of the perception of light that has been established through attention that has made it manifest, which suppresses sloth and torpor; and by means of non-distraction and composure which suppresses restlessness. Furthermore, that non-distraction of the mind, termed one-pointedness, by means of the in-breaths and out-breaths observing relinquishment, accomplished by mindfulness of breathing that has reached its peak and which suppresses all wrong thoughts, is the power of tranquility. This is the application of the meaning.

entries.pali: Kāmapaṭisaṃyutto vitakko kāmavitakko. Byāpādapaṭisaṃyutto vitakko byāpādavitakko. Vihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyutto vitakko vihiṃsāvitakko. Tesu dve sattesupi saṅkhāresupi uppajjanti. Kāmavitakko hi piye manāpe satte vā saṅkhāre vā vitakkentassa uppajjati. Byāpādavitakko appiye amanāpe satte vā saṅkhāre vā kujjhitvā olokanakālato paṭṭhāya yāva vināsanā uppajjati. Vihiṃsāvitakko saṅkhāresu nuppajjati. Saṅkhāro hi dukkhāpetabbo nāma natthi. Ime sattā haññantu vā ucchijjantu vā vinassantu vā mā vā ahesunti cintanakāle pana sattesu uppajjati.
entries.chinese_simplified: 与欲相应的寻是欲寻（kāmavitakka）。与瞋相应的寻是瞋寻（byāpādavitakka）。与害相应的寻是害寻（vihiṃsāvitakka）。此三者中，前两种寻于有情（satta）与行（saṅkhāra）两者中都会生起。欲寻于寻思可爱、合意的有情或行时生起。瞋寻于对不可爱、不合意的有情或行生气时，从看视之时起，乃至欲其毁灭时生起。害寻不在行中生起，因为行并无所谓‘可使其受苦’者。而当思惟‘愿这些有情被杀害、被断灭、被毁灭，或愿其不复存在！’时，害寻则于有情中生起。
entries.english: A thought connected with sensual pleasure is a 'sensual thought' (kāmavitakka). A thought connected with ill will is a 'thought of ill will' (byāpādavitakka). A thought connected with harming is a 'thought of harming' (vihiṃsāvitakka). Among these, two arise in regard to both beings and formations. Indeed, a sensual thought arises for one who is thinking about a being or a formation that is dear and agreeable. A thought of ill will arises from the moment of looking with anger at a being or a formation that is not dear and not agreeable, up until its destruction. A thought of harming does not arise in regard to formations. For indeed, there is no such thing as a formation that can be made to suffer. However, it arises in regard to beings at the time of thinking, "Let these beings be killed, or let them be cut off, or let them be destroyed, or may they not exist!"

entries.pali: 188 . ‘‘Tathā tatheva gadanato’’ ti iminā ‘‘tathāgato’’ti āmeḍitalopenāyaṃ niddesoti dasseti. Tathā tathevā ti ca dhammaatthasabhāvānurūpaṃ, veneyyajjhāsayānurūpañcāti adhippāyo. Diṭṭhanti rūpāyatanaṃ daṭṭhabbato, tena yaṃ diṭṭhaṃ, yaṃ dissati, yaṃ dakkhati, yaṃ sati samavāye passeyyaṃ, taṃ sabbaṃ ‘‘diṭṭhaṃ’’ tveva gahitaṃ kālavisesassa anāmaṭṭhabhāvato. ‘‘Suta’’ ntiādīsupi eseva nayo. Sutanti saddāyatanaṃ sotabbato. Muta nti sanissayena ghānādiindriyena sayaṃ patvā pāpuṇitvā gahetabbaṃ. Tenāha ‘‘patvā gahetabbato’’ ti. Viññāta nti vijānitabbaṃ, taṃ pana diṭṭhādivinimuttaṃ viññeyyanti āha ‘‘sukhadukkhādidhammāyatana’’ nti. Patta nti yathā tathā pattaṃ, hatthagataṃ adhigatanti attho. Tenāha ‘‘pariyesitvā vā apariyesitvā vā’’ ti. Pariyesita nti pattiyāmatthaṃ pariyiṭṭhaṃ, taṃ pana pattaṃ vā siyā appattaṃ vā ubhayathāpi pariyesitamevāti āha ‘‘pattaṃ vā appattaṃ vā’’ ti. Padadvayenāpi dvippakārampi pattaṃ, dvippakārampi pariyesitaṃ, tena tena pakārena tathāgatena abhisambuddhanti dasseti. Cittena anusañcarita nti copanaṃ apāpetvā citteneva anusaṃcaritaṃ, parivitakkitanti attho. Pītakanti ādī ti ādi -saddena lohitakaodātādi sabbaṃ rūpārammaṇavibhāgaṃ saṅgaṇhāti. Sumano ti rāgavasena, lobhavasena, saddhādivasena vā sumano. Dummano ti byāpādavitakkavasena, vihiṃsāvitakkavasena vā dummano. Majjhatto ti aññāṇavasena vā ñāṇavasena vā majjhatto. Eseva nayo sabbattha. Tattha tattha ādi -saddena saṅkhasaddo paṇavasaddo, pattagandho pupphagandho, pattaraso phalaraso, upādinnaṃ anupādinnaṃ, majjhattavedanā kusalakammaṃ akusalakammanti evaṃ ādīnaṃ saṅgaho daṭṭhabbo.
entries.chinese_simplified: 188. ‘如其所如而言说故’，以此显示‘如来’(tathāgato)一词是经由叠词省略而作的解释(niddesa)。‘如其所如’的意趣是，既符合法的义理与自性，也符合所教化者的意乐。‘所见’(diṭṭha)，指色处(rūpāyatana)，因其可被见；由此，凡是已见、正见、当见，或当因缘和合时可见者，皆总括为‘所见’，因其不涉及时间的差别。‘所闻’(suta)等也是同样的道理。‘所闻’，指声处(saddāyatana)，因其可被听。‘所觉’(muta)，指依靠鼻根等感官，自身到达、触及而领受者。因此说‘因触及而领受故’。‘所识’(viññāta)，指应被识知者；但它是有别于所见等的所知，因此说‘苦、乐等法处(dhammāyatana)’。‘所得’(patta)，指如其所得，意即到手、已证得。因此说‘或经由遍求，或未经遍求’。‘所遍求’(pariyesita)，指为得而遍求；此或已得，或未得，两种情况都名为‘所遍求’，因此说‘或已得，或未得’。此二词显示了两种‘所得’与两种‘所遍求’，如来通过这些方式完全证悟。‘以心随行’，指不令（身）动，仅以心随行，意即思量。‘黄色’等，此中‘等’字，总括了红色、白色等一切色所缘的分别。‘悦意’(sumano)，指因贪欲、贪婪或信心等而心悦。‘不悦’(dummano)，指因瞋寻或害寻而心不悦。‘中舍’(majjhatto)，指因无知或智慧而住于中舍。此理于一切处皆然。各处所说‘等’字，当知总括了螺声、鼓声，叶香、花香，叶味、果味，有取、无取，舍受，善业、不善业等。
entries.english: 188. "Thus, indeed, by speaking" — this shows that the designation "Tathāgata" is indicated through the elision of repetition. "Thus, indeed" means in accordance with the nature of the Dhamma and its meaning, and in accordance with the disposition of those to be taught — this is the intention. "Seen" refers to the visible object, as it is to be seen. Whatever was seen, whatever is seen, whatever will be seen, whatever one might see when the conditions are present — all that is included under "seen," because the distinction of time is not considered. The same applies to "heard," etc. "Heard" refers to the audible object, as it is to be heard. "Sensed" refers to what is to be grasped by the faculty of smell, etc., along with its basis, by reaching and attaining it directly. Hence it is said, "by reaching and grasping." "Known" refers to what is to be cognized. But this is distinct from the seen, heard, and sensed, so it is called "the knowable," referring to the objects of mind such as pleasure and pain. "Attained" means attained in whatever way, come to hand, acquired. Hence it is said, "whether sought after or not sought after." "Sought after" means searched for the sake of attainment. Whether attained or not attained, both are still "sought after." Thus, by these two terms, two kinds of attainment and two kinds of seeking are shown, indicating how the Tathāgata has fully awakened to them in every way. "Traversed by mind" means traversed by the mind alone, without agitation—that is, pondered. "Yellow, etc." — the word "etc." includes all divisions of visible objects, such as red, white, etc. "Glad" means joyful due to lust, greed, faith, etc. "Sorrowful" means distressed due to ill will, harmful thoughts, etc. "Neutral" means indifferent due to ignorance or knowledge. The same applies everywhere. Here, the word "etc." should be understood to include sounds like conch-shells and drums, smells like leaf-scents and flower-scents, tastes like leaf-tastes and fruit-tastes, the clung-to and the unclung-to, neutral feeling, wholesome and unwholesome kamma, and so forth.

entries.pali: Nanu ca alobhādosānaṃ aññamaññāvirahato tesaṃ vasena uppajjanakānaṃ imesaṃ nekkhammavitakkādīnaṃ aññamaññaṃ asaṅkaraṇato vavatthānaṃ na hotīti? Noti dassetuṃ ‘‘yadā’’ tiādi āraddhaṃ. Alobho sīsaṃ hotī ti alobho padhāno hoti. Niyamitapariṇatasamudācārādivasena yadā alobhappadhāno nekkhammagaruko cittuppādo hoti, tadā laddhāvasaro nekkhammavitakko patiṭṭhahati. Taṃsampayuttassa pana adosalakkhaṇassa abyāpādassa vasena yo tasseva abyāpādavitakkabhāvo sambhaveyya, sati ca abyāpādavitakkabhāve kassacipi aviheṭhanajātikatāya avihiṃsāvitakkabhāvo ca sambhaveyya, te itare dve. Tadanvayikā ti tasseva nekkhammavitakkassa anugāmino, sarūpato adissanato ‘‘tasmiṃ sati honti , asati na hontī’’ti tadanumānaneyyā bhavanti. Sesadvayepi iminā nayena attho veditabbo. Vuttanayenevā ti ‘‘kāmapaṭisaṃyutto saṅkappo kāmasaṅkappo’’ tiādinā vitakkattike vuttanayeneva (dī. ni. 3.288) veditabbo atthato abhinnattā. Yadi evaṃ kasmā puna desanā katāti? Tathā desanāya bujjhanakānaṃ ajjhāsayavasena desanāmattamevetaṃ.
entries.chinese_simplified: 难道因为无贪、无瞋彼此不相离，由它们所生起的离欲寻等，也会互相混杂而无法分辨吗？为了说明‘并非如此’，才开始说‘当……时’等。‘无贪为首’即无贪是主要的。由于其已确立、成熟的行相等，当以无贪为主、重视离欲的心生起时，得到机会的离欲寻就会安住。然而，就与此相应的、具有无瞋特相的无瞋而言，其无瞋寻的状态是可能存在的；并且，当无瞋寻存在时，由于其不伤害任何事物的本性，无害寻的状态也可能存在。此即其余二者。它们是随顺于彼离欲寻的，因其自性不可见，故应由‘彼在则有，彼无则无’来推断。其余二者也应依此理了知其义。‘已说之理’是指，应依寻三法聚中所说的‘与欲相应的思惟是欲思惟’等理(DN 3.288)来了知，因为义理上并无不同。若尔，为何要再次宣说呢？这仅仅是说法而已，是为了随顺那些能通过此种说法而觉悟者的意乐。
entries.english: Is it not the case that since non-greed and non-hatred are inseparable, and since these thoughts of renunciation and so on arise by means of them, there can be no clear distinction among them without confusion? To show that this is not so, the passage beginning with 'when' is introduced. 'Non-greed is the head' means non-greed is the principal factor. When, due to restrained and mature conduct and so on, a state of consciousness arises that is predominantly non-greedy and inclined toward renunciation, then, having found its opportunity, the thought of renunciation is established. Furthermore, through the influence of non-ill will, which is characterized by non-hatred and is associated with that thought, a state of being a thought of non-ill will may arise. And when there is a thought of non-ill will, due to its nature of not harming anyone, a state of being a thought of non-cruelty may also arise. These are the other two. 'They follow accordingly' means they are followers of that very thought of renunciation. Because they are not discernible in their own nature, they are to be inferred from it, according to the principle: 'When this is present, they are present; when it is absent, they are not.' The meaning of the remaining two should be understood in the same way. 'By the method already stated' means it should be understood by the method stated in the triad of thoughts, beginning with 'intention connected with sensuality is sensual intention' (Dī. Ni. 3.288), for in essence they are not different. If so, why was the teaching given again? This is merely a teaching given according to the disposition of those who understand it in that way.

entries.pali: Ñāṇassa tikkhabhāvo nāma savisesaṃ paṭipakkhasamucchindanena veditabboti ‘‘khippaṃ kilese chindatīti tikkhapaññā’’ ti vatvā te pana kilese vibhāgena dassento, ‘‘uppannaṃ kāmavitakka’’ ntiādimāha. Samathavipassanāhi vikkhambhanatadaṅgavasena pahīnampi ariyamaggena asamūhatattā uppattidhammataṃ anatītatāya asamūhatuppannanti vuccati, taṃ idha ‘‘uppanna’’ nti adhippetaṃ. Nādhivāsetī ti santānaṃ āropetvā na vāseti. Pajahatī ti samucchedavasena pajahati. Vinodetī ti khipati. Byantiṃ karotī ti vigatantaṃ karoti. Anabhāvaṃ gametī ti anu abhāvaṃ gameti, vipassanākkamena ariyamaggaṃ patvā samucchedavaseneva abhāvaṃ gamayatīti attho. Ettha ca kāmappaṭisaṃyutto vitakko kāmavitakko . ‘‘Ime sattā marantū’’ti paresaṃ maraṇappaṭisaṃyutto vitakko byāpādavitakko . ‘‘Ime sattā vihiṃsiyantū’’ti paresaṃ vihiṃsāpaṭisaṃyutto vitakko vihiṃsāvitakko. Pāpake ti lāmake. Akusale dhamme ti akosallasambhūte dhamme. Tikkhapañño nāma khippābhiñño hoti, paṭipadā cassa na calatīti āha – ‘‘ekamhi āsane cattāro ariyamaggā’’ tiādi.
entries.chinese_simplified: 所谓智(ñāṇa)的锐利性(tikkhabhāva)，当知是由于能特别地正断敌对法。说到“能迅速斩断诸烦恼，故为锐慧(tikkhapaññā)”，为分别开示那些烦恼，而说“已生起的欲寻(kāmavitakka)”等。虽已通过止(samatha)与观(vipassanā)，以镇伏断(vikkhambhana-pahāna)及彼分断(tadaṅga-pahāna)的方式断除，但因未被圣道(ariyamagga)根除，未超越其生起之法性，故说为“未根除而生起”，此处的“已生起”即是此意。“不容忍(nādhivāseti)”是指不让其在心相续中安住。“舍弃(pajahati)”是指以正断断(samuccheda-pahāna)的方式舍弃。“遣除(vinodeti)”是指驱逐。“令其终结(byantiṃ karoti)”是指使其灭绝。“令其无有(anabhāvaṃ gameti)”是指使其趋向于无，意即通过观的次第，到达圣道，以正断断的方式使其不存在。此处，与欲相应的寻(vitakka)是欲寻；“愿此等众生死去”是与他人死亡相应的寻，即是瞋寻(byāpādavitakka)；“愿此等众生受伤害”是与伤害他人相应的寻，即是害寻(vihiṃsāvitakka)。“诸恶(pāpake)”即是诸卑劣法。“诸不善法(akusale dhamme)”即是由不善巧所生起的法。锐慧者是速通达者(khippābhiñña)，其行道(paṭipadā)不动摇，故说“于一座中证四圣道”等。
entries.english: The sharpness of wisdom (ñāṇa) is to be understood by way of the special cutting off of the opponents, as it is said: "One with sharp wisdom (tikkhapaññā) quickly cuts off defilements." Then, to explain those defilements in detail, he begins with "arisen sensual thought," and so on. Even though defilements are abandoned through suppression (vikkhambhana) or temporary abandonment (tadaṅga) by tranquility (samatha) and insight (vipassanā), they are not eradicated by the noble path and thus remain capable of arising again, not transcending the nature of origination. Hence, being not eradicated but arisen, they are called "arisen," which is what is meant by "arisen" in this context. "Does not tolerate" (nādhivāseti) means one does not let them dwell after they have arisen in the mental continuum. "Abandons" (pajahati) means abandoning them through eradication (samuccheda). "Dispels" (vinodeti) means casting them away. "Brings to an end" (byantiṃ karoti) means makes them gone to an end. "Annihilates" (anabhāvaṃ gameti) means causes to go to non-existence successively; the meaning is that by the stages of insight, having attained the noble path, one causes them to go to non-existence by way of eradication. Here, a thought connected with sensuality is a sensual thought (kāmavitakka). A thought connected with the death of others, such as "May these beings die," is a thought of ill will (byāpādavitakka). A thought connected with harming others, such as "May these beings be harmed," is a thought of harm (vihiṃsāvitakka). "Evil" (pāpaka) refers to what is base. "Unskillful states" (akusale dhamme) are those born of unskillfulness. One with sharp wisdom is one who quickly comprehends, and his practice does not waver, as stated: "In one sitting, the four noble paths," etc.

entries.pali: Sattadhammādhiṭṭhānaṃ pucchaṃ nīharitvā pucchāvicayo ācariyena vibhatto, amhehi ca ñāto, ‘‘tassaṃ pucchāyaṃ katamā vissajjanāgāthā’’ti pucchitabbattā ‘‘tattha vissajjanā’’ tiādi āraddhaṃ. Tatthā ti tassaṃ gāthāyaṃ. ‘‘Kāmesu…pe… paribbaje’’ti vissajjanā gāthā bhagavatā vuttā. Kāmesū ti kāmīyantīti kāmā, tesu kāmesu. Vatthukāmesu kilesakāmena paṇḍitehi nābhigijjheyya. Manasā nāvilosiyā ti āvilabhāvakare byāpādavitakkādayo ceva kāyaduccaritādayo ca dhamme pajahanto paṇḍito manasā anāvilo suppasanno bhaveyya. Kusalo sabbadhammāna nti sabbadhammānaṃ aniccatādinā paritulitattā aniccatādīsu pañcasu khandhesu kusalo cheko. Sato ti kesādīsu saratīti sato. Bhikkhū ti saṅkhatadhamme bhayādito ikkhatīti bhikkhu. Paribbaje ti tadaṅgavikkhambhanasamucchedappahānabhāvena kilesakāmavatthukāme pari samantato vajjeyya.
entries.chinese_simplified: 提出七法依处(Sattadhammādhiṭṭhāna)之问后，阿阇梨已分析此问之审查，我等亦已知晓。因当问‘于此问，何为解答偈？’，故开始‘于此解答’等语。‘于此’者，即于此偈中。‘于欲……乃至……应遍行’是世尊所说之解答偈。‘于欲’者，谓被欲求故为欲，于此等欲中。智者不应以烦恼欲贪求事物欲。‘心不扰乱’者，谓智者舍离能令心生扰乱之瞋寻等及身恶行等法，心应无扰乱、极清净。‘善巧一切法’者，因以无常等称量一切法，故于无常等五蕴中善巧、练达。‘具念’者，于发等中忆念故为具念者。‘比丘’者，于有为法中见怖畏等故为比丘。‘应遍行’者，以彼分断、镇伏断、究竟断之方式，应周遍舍离烦恼欲与事物欲。
entries.english: Having extracted the question concerning the Dhamma with seven bases, the analysis of the question was explained by the teacher, and it is known by us. Because it is to be asked, 'In that question, what is the reply verse?', the passage beginning 'therein, the reply' was started. 'Therein' means in that verse. 'In sensual pleasures... let him wander forth'—this is the reply verse spoken by the Blessed One. 'In sensual pleasures' means those things that are desired are sensual pleasures; in those sensual pleasures. Regarding sensual objects, a wise person should not be greedy through the defilement of desire. 'With mind unclouded'—by abandoning states which cause agitation, such as thoughts of ill-will and bodily misconduct, the wise one should be unclouded in mind, very serene. 'Skilled in all phenomena'—because all phenomena are weighed by way of impermanence and so on, one is skilled in the five aggregates with regard to impermanence and so on. 'Mindful'—one is mindful because one is mindful of the parts of the body, beginning with the hair of the head. 'A bhikkhu'—one is a bhikkhu because one sees conditioned phenomena as fearful and so on. 'Let him wander forth'—one should completely avoid the defilements of sensual pleasure and the objects of sensual pleasure by way of abandonment by substitution of opposites, abandonment by suppression, and abandonment by cutting off.

entries.pali: Jhānasambhārā nekkhammavitakko sambhāro kāmavitakkavinodanādhippāyatā. Abyāpādavitakko sambhāro byāpādavitakkapaṭivinodanādhippāyatā. Avihiṃsāvitakko sambhāro vihiṃsāvitakkapaṭivinodanādhippāyatā. Indriyesu guttadvāratā appicchatā sambhāro parisuddhājīvo catunnaṃ samāpattīnaṃ sambhāro akammassa vihāritā. Maggasambhāro samāpattipajjanatā. Phalasambhāro jhānanibbattitāya jhānasamudāgamo. Kusalahetu yaṃ jhānaṃ samudayaṃ gacchanti ko ca koci (ka.) na kutoci nekkhammappattā samudāgacchanti. Ālambanirodhasamādhi santo samudāgacchanti. Avītikkantā samudāgacchanti. Sukhindriyaṃ somanassindriyaṃ pahānāya te ca abyāpajjatāya samudāgacchanti. Taṃ pana sandhāya samudāgacchanti. Aparidāhanāya samudāgacchanti. Ayaṃ ñāṇasamudāgamo.
entries.chinese_simplified: 禅那的资粮：出离寻(nekkhamma-vitakka)是资粮，意在遣除欲寻(kāma-vitakka)；无瞋寻(abyāpāda-vitakka)是资粮，意在遣除瞋寻(byāpāda-vitakka)；无害寻(avihiṃsā-vitakka)是资粮，意在遣除害寻(vihiṃsā-vitakka)。于诸根守护门、少欲、清净活命是四种等至(samāpatti)的资粮，以及住于无为。道资粮是达成等至。果资粮是因禅那成就而有的禅那现起。以善为因，禅那得以生起；已达出离者，其生起非来自任何处。所缘灭尽之定，显现而生起。未超越（禅、道、果）而生起。为舍断乐根与喜根，为无恼害而生起。又，依于彼（舍断）而生起。为无遍烧恼而生起。此是智的现起。
entries.english: The requisites for jhāna: the requisite of the thought of renunciation is the intention to dispel sensual thought. The requisite of the thought of non-ill-will is the intention to dispel the thought of ill-will. The requisite of the thought of non-harming is the intention to dispel the thought of harming. Guardedness in the sense faculties, fewness of wishes, and pure livelihood are requisites. The requisite of the four attainments is dwelling in inaction. The requisite of the path is the attainment of absorption. The requisite of fruition, due to the production of jhāna, is the arising of jhāna. It is from a wholesome cause that jhānas come to arise. Some, having attained renunciation, do not arise from any cause. The concentration of the cessation of the object, being peaceful, arises. Not having been transgressed, they arise. For the abandoning of the faculty of pleasure and the faculty of joy, they arise through non-affliction. Referring to that very abandoning, they arise. They arise for the sake of non-feverishness. This is the arising of knowledge.

entries.pali: Tattha katamā bhāvanā? Mettāsevanā abyāpādavitakkabhāvanā. Karuṇāsevanā avihiṃsāvitakkabhāvanā. Muditābhāvanā pītisukhasampajaññā kāritā. Upekkhābhāvanā passavatā upekkhābhāvanā apassavatā upekkhā ca ajjhupekkhā ca, asubhasaññābhāvanā dukkhāpaṭipadā dandhābhiññā bhavasandhābhiññā bhavasandhānaṃ, sā chabbidhā bhāvanā bhāvitā bahulīkatā anuṭṭhitā vatthukatā yānīkatā paricitā susamāraddhā. Ayaṃ bhāvanā.
entries.chinese_simplified: 于此，何为修习？修习慈，是无瞋寻的修习。修习悲，是无害寻的修习。修习喜，是令喜、乐、正知行作。修习舍，有见者之修习与无见者之修习，亦即是舍与近舍(ajjhupekkhā)。修习不净想(asubha-saññā)，是苦行道(dukkhāpaṭipadā)、慢通达(dandhābhiññā)、连结有之通达，以及有之连结。彼六种修习，已修习、多作、已勤修、已作基础、已作车乘、已熟习、已善策励。此即是修习。
entries.english: Herein, what is development? The cultivation of loving-kindness is the development of the thought of non-ill-will. The cultivation of compassion is the development of the thought of non-harming. The development of appreciative joy brings about the clear comprehension of rapture and happiness. The development of equanimity is for one who sees, and the development of equanimity is for one who does not see; it is both equanimity and onlooking equanimity. The development of the perception of foulness is of painful progress and slow direct knowledge, the direct knowledge that connects existence, the connecting of existence. That sixfold development is developed, frequently practiced, repeatedly undertaken, made a foundation, made a vehicle, familiarized, and well undertaken. This is development.
